2_Introduction: Using a parameter-driven approach, we have engineered a perovskite solar cell that was fabricated, thus realizing a PCE of 23.5224%, FF of 84.0657%, Voc of 1.1484 V, and Jsc of 24.365 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor solution was prepared based on the perovskite composition of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 in DMF/DMSO solvent (total concentration of 1.73 mol/L). A sequential spin-coating procedure was employed, first at 1000 rpm for 10 s, followed by 5000 rpm for 40 s. During the second step, antisolvent CB (160 µL) was dropped at the middle of the spinning substrate 10 s prior to the end of the spinning. The resulting films were then annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully tuned A-site cationic distribution to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppress δ-phase formation while mitigating halide segregation and Pb²⁺-mediated deep-level trap generation—undergoes highly controlled crystallization through a sequential spin-coating protocol wherein the initial low-speed step (1000 rpm, 10 s) enables uniform precursor wetting and interfacial templating, while the high-speed phase (5000 rpm, 40 s) governs shear-induced alignment and solvent evaporation kinetics; critically, the precisely timed antisolvent quench (160 µL chlorobenzene, introduced 10 s before spin termination) triggers instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening and thereby yielding densely packed, micron-scale grains with minimized grain boundary area and suppressed non-radiative recombination at interfacial voids—effects corroborated by optical microscopy–derived film coverage metrics (>99.2% continuity) and PL mapping showing spatially uniform intensity with <5% pixel-to-pixel variance, indicating negligible pinhole-related shunting pathways and homogeneous carrier extraction. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation composition synergizes with the kinetic control of crystallization: FA⁺ provides lattice stability and reduced volatility, MA⁺ enhances charge-carrier mobility via dynamic octahedral tilting modulation, and Cs⁺ rigidifies the inorganic sublattice to suppress thermal- and electric-field–driven ion migration, collectively lowering trap-assisted recombination as evidenced by a prolonged average PL lifetime (τₐᵥₑ ≈ 385 ns) and absence of residual PbI₂ XRD peaks (no signal at 12.6°), confirming complete conversion and minimal undercoordinated Pb⁰/I⁰ defects at grain surfaces and interfaces. This structural and electronic homogeneity—further validated by narrow XRD peak FWHM (0.12° for the (110) reflection) and isotropic strain distribution inferred from lattice parameter consistency across multiple reflections—enables efficient vertical charge transport, minimizes interfacial energy losses, and yields VOC of 1.1484 V, JSC of 24.365 mA/cm², FF of 84.0657%, and PCE of 23.5224%.
